subject: Partially observed data for large sets

messages.author: ee490f1373633c05
messages.subject: Partially observed data for large sets
parts:
Hi all,

The STAN users manual and STAN examples give examples of how you code the situation where some observations are observed and some are not.  However, to do this, the index number for each observation is specified manually. 

I am looking at a time series of thousands of data points.  In JAGS, the observed/not observed distinction is easily handled simply by passing NAs for unobserved values.  Is there a similar feature or way of doing this in STAN? I don't want to have to write thousands of lines of code to do this manually...

Thanks

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Partially observed data for large sets
parts:
On Saturday, March 15, 2014 6:45:17 PM UTC-4, Julian King wrote:
The STAN users manual and STAN examples give examples of how you code the situation where some observations are observed and some are not.  However, to do this, the index number for each observation is specified manually. 

I am looking at a time series of thousands of data points.  In JAGS, the observed/not observed distinction is easily handled simply by passing NAs for unobserved values.  Is there a similar feature or way of doing this in STAN? I don't want to have to write thousands of lines of code to do this manually...

There is no NA for data in Stan. You can recode the missing values as sum magic number that does not otherwise occur in the observed data, such as -999, and then write your .stan file to have a bunch of clauses like

if (y[i] == -999) {
  // do something
}
else {
  // do something else
}

But it is pretty tedious to deal with non-trivial missing data patterns in Stan.

Ben
